prompt: A population of $2{,}000$ bacteria doubles every $5$ hours. Which function models the population $P$ after $t$ hours?
hint: The base is the growth factor ($2$ for doubling). The exponent must count how many doublings have happened.

hints.text: The base is the growth factor ($2$ for doubling). The exponent must count how many doublings have happened.
After $t$ hours, the number of $5$-hour periods that have elapsed is $t/5$.

learningObjective: Build an exponential model when the period differs from the time unit.
explanation: The exponent must count doublings, not hours. In $t$ hours there are $\dfrac{t}{5}$ five-hour periods.
So $P = 2000(2)^{t/5}$. Check at $t = 5$: $2000 \cdot 2^1 = 4000$ ✓ — exactly one doubling.

alternativeExplanations.title: Divide by the period, never multiply
steps: Choice A gives $2000 \cdot 2^{25}$ after 5 hours — astronomically wrong.
Whenever the growth period is longer than the time unit, the exponent divides.
The general form is $a \cdot b^{t/p}$, where $p$ is how long one full growth period takes. Test at $t = p$ to confirm you get exactly one growth step.
